title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): a 'disposition' is a set E with a relation V_E, which amounts to a strict graph. Write x|0|A for 'x is unrelated to (orthogonal to) every point of A'. Define cosupp°_E(B) = {x ∈ E | x|0|B}, the polar or orthogonal complement. Define supp°_E = cosupp°_E ∘ cosupp°_E, the double-polar closure. Σ_E is the set of closed subsets, the fixed points of supp°_E. On Σ_E the map C = cosupp° acts as an orthocomplementation, so Σ_E is the complete ortholattice of an orthogonality space (a Birkhoff polarity).

A morphism is a correspondence α: E → P(E'). It extends to unions, ᾱ(A) = ∪_{x∈A} α(x), and induces α_*: Σ_E → Σ_E' by α_*(S) = supp°_E'(ᾱ(S)). This map is defined for any correspondence.

When α is compatible with the dispositions, Grothendieck wants two formulas:
(*) α_*(supp°_E A) = supp°_E'(ᾱ(A)) for all A ⊂ E;
(**) α_*(cosupp°_E B) = cosupp°_E'(ᾱ(B)) for all B ⊂ E.
On page 60 compatibility is used in the form x|0|y ⇒ α(x)|0|α(y).

Crossed-out attempt at (*): put Ā = supp°A. The inclusion ⊃ follows from monotonicity. For ⊂ he would need x'|0|ᾱ(A) ⇒ x'|0|ᾱ(Ā). He sees no reason for this and writes 'ça doit être faux !'.

He then changes strategy and obtains (*) as a special case of the 'dual' formula (**), applied twice: once with B and once with B = cosupp°A. The chain is:
- α_*(supp°A) = α_*(cosupp°(cosupp°A)) = cosupp°(ᾱ(cosupp°A)).
- Polars do not change under closure, so this equals cosupp°(supp°ᾱ(cosupp°A)) = cosupp°(α_*(cosupp°A)).
- By (**) again, α_*(cosupp°A) = cosupp°ᾱ(A), so the whole equals cosupp°cosupp°ᾱ(A) = supp°ᾱ(A).

This derivation is valid given (**). The next page draws the consequence α_*(CB) = Cα_*(B): α_* commutes with orthocomplementation. It identifies (**) as the key formula and starts proving its ⊂ half from compatibility.

Overall this is a functoriality study: when does a morphism of orthogonality spaces induce an ortholattice morphism on the lattices of closed (biorthogonal) subsets?
errors: The transcription's 'ᾱ(Ā) ⊃ ᾱ(Ā)' should read ᾱ(Ā) ⊃ ᾱ(A). This is a slip in the transcription; the handwriting appears to read correctly.
(**) cannot follow from the stated compatibility (x|0|y ⇒ α(x)|0|α(y)) alone. Take α(x) = ∅ for all x: then α_*(cosupp° B) = supp°(∅) = cosupp°(E'), while cosupp°(ᾱ(B)) = cosupp°(∅) = E'.

A second counterexample is the inclusion of a sub-orthogonality-space. It is compatible, but in general the closure in E' of B^⊥∩E differs from the polar of B taken in E'. So the 'formule-clef' needs an extra surjectivity or density hypothesis on α. This page does not yet state one; whether later pages add it is unknown.

ideas.what: A set with an orthogonality ('disposition') relation; closed subsets as double polars; the complete ortholattice Σ_E with complement C = cosupp°
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonality spaces / orthoframes; Galois polarity; biorthogonal closure

ideas.what: A morphism given by a correspondence E → P(E'), with induced map α_* on closed sets; the question of when α_* commutes with closure and orthocomplement
ideas.modern_name: Morphisms of orthogonality spaces inducing ortholattice homomorphisms (cf. Moore's categorical duality for property lattices, Faure–Frölicher)

ideas.what: Reduction of the closure-compatibility formula (*) to the polar formula (**) by applying (**) twice

missed.claim: In 1986 Grothendieck independently sets up the category of orthogonality spaces ('dispositions'), with correspondence morphisms. He seeks conditions under which they induce orthocomplement-preserving maps of the closure lattices. This is the framework of quantum-logic property lattices (Foulis–Randall, Moore, Paseka–Vetterlein), which he does not appear to cite or know.
missed.quote: Il faut donc prouver (**), qui apparaît comme la formule-clef
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mostly of historical interest: it shows Grothendieck's late notes touching orthogonality/ortholattice structures. Mathematically the content is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine Galois-polarity manipulations within an apparently idiosyncratic 'disposition' framework. The material is already known in the orthogonality-space and quantum-logic literature, and the key formula still lacks a needed hypothesis.
